merger_name: National Dental Care – business assets comprising the BDF Dental clinic, Beaudesert, Queensland
merger_description:
NDC HoldCo Pty Ltd (together with its subsidiaries, **NDC**), through its wholly-owned subsidiary, NDC Australia Pty Limited, proposes to acquire from BDF Dental Pty Ltd 100% of the business assets comprising the BDF Dental clinic (**BDF Dental**).

NDC is a dental services organisation that operates a network of dental clinics that provide a range of general dentistry services. NDC has dental clinics in all Australian states and territories, including Queensland.

BDF Dental is a dental clinic located in Beaudesert, Queensland that provides a range of general dentistry services.

determination_table_content.details:
NDC Australia Pty Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of NDC
HoldCo Pty Ltd (together, National Dental Care), applied for a
notification waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of 100% of
the business assets comprising BDF Dental Pty Ltd (BDF Dental), as
described in the transaction documents provided as part of the
application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, National Dental Care, is a dental services organisation
that operates a network of dental clinics that provide a range of
general dentistry services. National Dental Care has dental clinics in
all Australian states and territories, including Queensland. National
Dental Care is majority owned by funds managed by Crescent Capital
Partners, an Australian private equity firm.
The target, BDF Dental, is a dental clinic located in Beaudesert,
Queensland that provides a range of general dentistry services.
National Dental Care and BDF Dental both supply general dentistry
services in Queensland.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between National Dental Care
and BDF Dental in the supply of general dentistry services in
the local area surrounding BDF Dental
b. there are alternative suppliers of general dentistry services in
Beaudesert and the surrounding areas.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
